title: Harness² source code is available under Apache-2.0
summary: The public repository includes a local deterministic demo and documented setup for model-backed benchmark runs.
research_notes:
On Linux with Python 3.12 and uv, create the documented virtual environment, install the editable package, and run the credential-free demo before connecting a model.

For a model-backed run, install the listed runtime and benchmark dependencies, configure model settings and authentication, then start with one benchmark task and a small selection.

Run checking, refinement, judging, and reporting with identical benchmark, executor, subset, recursion budget, mode, and seed; use dry-run to inspect task selection without model calls.

Choose parallel recursion to explore candidate harnesses more widely, or sequential recursion to carry refinements through successive steps; retain adopted harnesses only with their supporting execution evidence.

Configure network restrictions before evaluation so public benchmark rubrics, answers, or grading criteria cannot leak into an executor with unrestricted web access.

Keep the evaluation configuration identical to the refinement run when judging and reporting; changing the benchmark, executor, subset, recursion mode, budget, or seed invalidates a like-for-like result.

Treat larger recursion budgets as an explicit compute–performance trade-off: the paper counts both execution and improvement tokens, and its gains were measured only in the evaluated benchmark configurations.
